description:
Analyze real estate development feasibility in San Francisco using parcel and zoning data.

Task: Using Jupyter Lab, analyze which San Francisco parcels are feasible for new residential development based on zoning constraints and current building utilization.

REQUIREMENTS:
- Open the Jupyter notebook at /home/ga/urbansim_projects/notebooks/development_feasibility.ipynb
- Load the 'parcels', 'buildings', and 'zoning' tables from /home/ga/urbansim_projects/data/sanfran_public.h5
- Join parcels to zoning data. First check if parcels has a 'zoning_id' column; if so, use it to join to the zoning table index. If not, load the 'zoning_for_parcels' table which maps parcel indices to zoning indices
- For each parcel, aggregate total building_sqft from the buildings table (group by parcel_id and sum building_sqft)
- Calculate current FAR (floor area ratio) as total_building_sqft / (shape_area * 10.764), where shape_area is in square meters and 10.764 converts to square feet
- Compare current FAR against the maximum allowed FAR from zoning (max_far)
- Identify parcels where current FAR is less than 50% of max_far as 'development feasible'
- Create a summary showing: total parcels, feasible parcels, percentage feasible, average unused capacity
- Save a CSV of the top 100 most feasible parcels (by unused capacity ratio) to /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/feasible_parcels.csv with columns including: parcel_id, current_density, max_allowed, unused_capacity_ratio
- Create a bar chart showing the distribution of unused capacity ratios across all feasible parcels and save to /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/feasibility_distribution.png

The notebook should be executed with all cells run.
